competences: The learner identifies signs that guide road users.
The learner connects a zebra crossing with safe road crossing.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads, spells and writes: road, sign, stop, school, zebra, crossing, parking.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify three named signs on the classroom chart.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to state one importance of road signs.
priorKnowledge: Learners have identified people and vehicles that use roads; they now identify signs that guide those road users.
materials: Road-sign chart with stop, school ahead, zebra crossing, railway crossing and no parking
Word cards matching the five displayed road signs
references: P I Literacy Scheme OF Work Term III
P I Literacy Lesson Notes Term III

steps.content: Transport pictures and the starter question: Write any one importance of road signs to road users.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays road-sign chart with stop, school ahead, zebra crossing, railway crossing and no parking and asks: "Write any one importance of road signs to road users." Learners first identify familiar pictures; the teacher connects their responses to road signs.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners look at the transport pictures, identify familiar words, and give oral responses to the starter question before copying any notes.

steps.content: Meaning of road signs: Road signs are symbols put on roads to guide road users.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Road signs are symbols put on roads to guide road users. Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Write any one importance of road signs to road users." and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for meaning of road signs, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

steps.content: Signs on the road: Stop School ahead Zebra crossing Railway crossing No parking
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Stop School ahead Zebra crossing Railway crossing No parking Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Why is it good for you to follow road signs?" and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for signs on the road, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

steps.content: Importance of road signs: Road signs help to reduce traffic jams. Road signs help to reduce road accidents.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Road signs help to reduce traffic jams. Road signs help to reduce road accidents. Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "How is a zebra crossing useful to road users?" and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for importance of road signs, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

steps.content: Zebra crossing: A zebra crossing is a safe place for crossing a road.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: A zebra crossing is a safe place for crossing a road. Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Name the road signs shown on the classroom chart." and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for zebra crossing, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

steps.content: 1. Write any one importance of road signs to road users. 2. Why is it good for you to follow road signs? 3. How is a zebra crossing useful to road users? 4. Name the road signs shown on the classroom chart.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets the sourced exercise: "Write any one importance of road signs to road users." "Why is it good for you to follow road signs?" "How is a zebra crossing useful to road users?" "Name the road signs shown on the classroom chart." The teacher reads each item clearly, checks individual answers, and uses the transport chart to correct mistaken identifications.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the exercise questions in their books, complete any specified matching or drawing, and correct their responses with the teacher.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher checks the lesson objectives using these exercise items: "Write any one importance of road signs to road users." "Why is it good for you to follow road signs?" "How is a zebra crossing useful to road users?" The teacher confirms correct answers against the board notes and identifies learners needing further picture-supported practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give short oral answers, compare them with the transport pictures and board notes, and correct any remaining errors in their books.

assessment: Check the written exercise and oral responses: Write any one importance of road signs to road users. Why is it good for you to follow road signs? How is a zebra crossing useful to road users? Mark against the source-based answers and revisit incorrect identifications using the transport chart.
homework: Complete or correct this sourced exercise item in your book: Name the road signs shown on the classroom chart.
